questions_and_answers.question_text: What are the two usual translations of the auxiliary verb xiǎng?
Give the three possible translations of Wǒ xiǎng mǎi Yīngwén bào.
Write the Chinese for "I very much want to study."
What does tài mean, and in which unit does it appear?
Write the Chinese for "I would like to buy an English-language newspaper."
What kind of verb is xiǎng?
Write the Chinese for "I think he is planning to leave tomorrow."

answers.answer_text: Wǒ xiǎng tā xiǎng míngtian zǒu.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "I don't want to go very much."
In Wǒ xiǎng tā xiǎng míngtian zǒu, how is xiǎng used each time?

answers.answer_text: The first xiǎng is the main verb "to think that"; the second is the auxiliary verb "to want to / to be planning to."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give the Chinese reply meaning "Fine. They're right here."

articles.text:
3. A: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi Yīngwén bào.             I would like to buy an English-
                                            language newspaper.
   B: Hǎo. Jiù zài zhèli.                   Fine. They're right here.

Note on No. 3

The auxiliary verb xiǎng is sometimes translated as "would like to" or "to want to." Here are some examples of translations you have learned for xiǎng:

Wǒ xiǎng mǎi Yīngwén bào.        I'm thinking of buying an English-
                                 language newspaper. OR I would
                                 like to buy an English-language
                                 newspaper. OR I want to buy an
                                 English-language newspaper.

Wǒ xiǎng tā xiǎng míngtian       I think he is planning to leave
zǒu.                             tomorrow.

Wǒ hěn xiǎng niàn shū.           I very much want to study.

Wǒ bú tài xiǎng qù.              I don't want to go very much. [Tài,
                                 meaning "too," "excessively,"
                                 appears in Unit 3.]
